Establishes attribution for the ruler under evaluation. No substantive economic policy content; provides biographical grounding for all 5B questions.","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0002","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.1","5B.3"],"relevance_strength":"weak","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0001","unit-0003"],"explanation":"Describes AMLO's charismatic leadership, combative discourse, and political positioning against 'poderes fácticos' and neoliberal structural reforms (salinista and zedillista administrations). References his 2000 DF government tenure and videoescándalo. Political-context background rather than economic governance evidence.","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0003","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.1"],"relevance_strength":"weak","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0002","unit-0004"],"explanation":"Covers 2006 presidential election dispute. AMLO lost by 0.56%, claimed 'robo' (theft) of the election, launched civil disobedience campaign, and proclaimed himself 'president legítimo.' International community recognized Calderón. Electoral controversy and political legitimacy framing; no substantive economic governance content.","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0004","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.1","5B.3","5B.4"],"relevance_strength":"material","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0003","unit-0005"],"explanation":"Covers 2012 presidential bid and opposition to EPN's structural reforms (energy, education, labor, telecommunications). AMLO diagnosed Mexico under a 'régimen neoporfirista' of corruption, impunity, and privileges; promised to halt neoliberalism and protect Pemex from privatization. Direct evidence of economic policy stance, opposition to market-opening reforms, and prioritization of state-owned enterprises over private competition.","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0005","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.1","5B.2","5B.3","5B.5","5B.6","5B.8","5B.9"],"relevance_strength":"pivotal","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0004","unit-0006"],"explanation":"Presents the full 2018 electoral platform (Proyecto 2018 / Juntos Haremos Historia). Key economic policy content: 'austeridad republicana' to reorient public resources from current spending to investment without raising taxes; social programs targeting poverty and vulnerable groups; energy self-sufficiency; combating corruption 'dando ejemplo'; opposition to privatization of strategic sectors; 'producción nacional' prioritization. This is the most substantive economic policy platform statement in the document, directly addressing 5B.1 (prosperity agenda vs. rents), 5B.2 (institutional appointments), 5B.3 (fiscal discipline), 5B.6 (budget quality), 5B.8 (distribution), and 5B.9 (shock preparedness).","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0006","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.1","5B.2","5B.3","5B.5","5B.7"],"relevance_strength":"material","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0005","unit-0007"],"explanation":"Describes the start of the presidency on 1 December 2018. Key content: commitment to 'no traicionar al pueblo' while respecting legal order; plans for a 'Constitución Moral' guiding the 'Cuarta Transformación'; National Consultation on Priority Programs; National Peace and Security Plan including a National Guard and conditional amnesty for narcos. Describes platform as pragmatic social democracy accepting free-market orthodoxy while rejecting privatization and prioritizing national production. Anti-corruption messaging ('erradicación de la corrupción política dando ejemplo'). Relevant for 5B.1 (policy orientation), 5B.2 (team quality), 5B.3 (institutional approach), 5B.5 (anti-corruption commitment), and 5B.7 (consultation and participation processes).","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0007","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.1","5B.4","5B.9"],"relevance_strength":"material","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0006","unit-0008"],"explanation":"Covers USMCA trade agreement (replacement for NAFTA), which López Obrador considered beneficial, alongside migration tensions with US under Trump (caravanas, border closure threats). Relevant for 5B.4 (trade/investment framework) and 5B.9 (external shock management: trade renegotiation, migration pressure, border tariffs). Also touches on economic sovereignty and international economic relations.","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0008","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.1"],"relevance_strength":"weak","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0007","unit-0009"],"explanation":"Biographical early life: birth (1953), family background, move to Villahermosa, childhood tragedy (brother's accidental death), early influences (Benito Juárez, Marxist philosophy, baseball, Catholic serving). No economic governance content; provides biographical attribution only.","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0009","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"weak","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0008","unit-0010"],"explanation":"University enrollment at UNAM (1972), political socialization through PRI system, first campaign involvement (1976 for Carlos Pellicer). No substantive economic governance content; early political career background.","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0010","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"weak","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0009","unit-0011"],"explanation":"Career development: delegation at INI in La Chontalpa, teaching at Universidad Autónoma de Tabasco, marriage to Rocío Beltrán (three sons: José Ramón, Andrés Manuel, Gonzalo). No substantive economic governance content; career background attribution.","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0011","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"weak","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0010","unit-0012"],"explanation":"PR I functions under González Pedrero; published two historical books on Tabasco; graduated from UNAM with thesis on Mexican state formation (1821-1867); joined Corriente Democrática (1987). Political career context; no economic governance evidence.","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0012","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"weak","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0011","unit-0013"],"explanation":"1988 elections: joined FDN coalition supporting Cuauhtémoc Cárdenas for president; ran for Villahermosa governor but lost to Neme Castillo (81% for PRI); claimed massive fraud. Book 'Tabasco, víctima del fraude.' Electoral dispute background; no substantive economic governance content.","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0013","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.1"],"relevance_strength":"weak","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0012","unit-0014"],"explanation":"PRD founding (1989); PRD president in Tabasco; 'Éxodo por la democracia' march (1991-1992) protesting municipal election fraud in Tabasco and Veracruz; gained national recognition as combative tribune. Political mobilization background; marginally relevant to policy orientation through anti-fraud stance.","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0014","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.1"],"relevance_strength":"weak","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0013","unit-0015"],"explanation":"1994 Tabasco gubernatorial election: lost to Roberto Madrazo (38.7% vs 57.5%); challenged results, documented campaign finance violations, launched caravans and civil resistance. PRD's poor electoral performance nationally. Anti-fraud framing; no direct economic governance evidence.","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0015","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.1","5B.5"],"relevance_strength":"weak","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0014","unit-0016"],"explanation":"Elected PRD president (CEN) in July 1996 with 73.9%; published book 'Entre la historia y la esperanza: corrupción y lucha democrática en Tabasco' attacking Madrazo. Directly connects corruption critique to political struggle; weakly relevant to anti-corruption governance (5B.5) but limited substantive evidence on enforcement.","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0016","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.5"],"relevance_strength":"material","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0015","unit-0017"],"explanation":"Resigned PRD presidency (Sept 1999); published findings on FOBAPROA (Fondo Bancario de Protección al Ahorro) — a state fund used to rescue bank losses that López Obrador called 'el fraude más grande de la historia después de La Conquista' and 'abiertamente inconstitucional.' Directly addresses 5B.5 (anti-corruption enforcement and audit) and 5B.7 (reliable information and evaluation). Evidence of corruption critique and willingness to investigate financial sector rescue operations.","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0017","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"weak","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0016","unit-0018"],"explanation":"Won DF primary candidacy (Nov 1999) with 75.5% over four rivals; negotiated support from PRD factions. Electoral context; no substantive economic governance content.","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0018","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"weak","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0017","unit-0019"],"explanation":"July 2000 federal elections: López Obrador won DF governorship (34.5%, narrowly beating PAN's Santiago Creel) while Vicente Fox won presidency. Electoral outcome; no substantive economic governance content in this unit.","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0019","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.1","5B.6","5B.7","5B.8"],"relevance_strength":"material","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0018","unit-0020"],"explanation":"DF governance period (2000-2005): vigorous public works program; social protection programs including Pensión Universal Alimenticia para Adultos Mayores; commitment to accountability, transparency, and participatory democracy ('rendición regular de cuentas, la transparencia y la democracia participativa'). Opposition (PAN) accused government of populist spending and rising debt. Relevant for 5B.1 (social vs patronage spending), 5B.6 (budget quality/infrastructure), 5B.7 (transparency and accountability), and 5B.8 (social program distribution).","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0020","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.7"],"relevance_strength":"material","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0019","unit-0021"],"explanation":"Governance style: 'las mañaneras' — daily 6am press conferences that generated unusual media attention and set the national political agenda; characterized as a tribuno who connected with popular classes; limited rhetorical skill but effective communication. Directly relevant to 5B.7 (reliable information dissemination and transparency practices).","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0021","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.1","5B.6","5B.8"],"relevance_strength":"material","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0020","unit-0022"],"explanation":"DF governance outcomes: vigorous public works campaigns; social programs (Pensión Universal Alimenticia para Adultos Mayores highlighted again); government refused to implement Seguro Popular claiming DF already had free coverage. Opposition accused of populist budget management without concern for debt. Directly addresses 5B.1 (spending priorities), 5B.6 (infrastructure and service delivery), and 5B.8 (distribution of social programs to vulnerable groups).","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0022","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.5"],"relevance_strength":"material","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0021","unit-0023"],"explanation":"Videoescándalo (March 2004): Televisa broadcast clandestine videos of PRD officials (Gustavo Ponce, René Bejarano, Carlos Ímaz) engaged in gambling and money collection from businessman Carlos Ahumada. Direct evidence of corruption involving close associates of López Obrador. Charged with fraud and money laundering. Relevant for 5B.5 (anti-corruption enforcement against politically connected actors).","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0023","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.5"],"relevance_strength":"material","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0022","unit-0024"],"explanation":"Videoescándalo aftermath: PRD broken with implicated officials; Rosario Robles forced to leave party; Leonel Godoy apologized publicly. López Obrador's reaction was late and lukewarm; attributed scandal to 'conspiración' by Salinas, Fernández de Cevallos, and Fox. Key fact: 'costaba imaginar que López Obrador no estuviera al corriente' of Bejarano's activities given their close relationship. Relevant for 5B.5 (accountability and anti-corruption conduct by ruler's inner circle).","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0024","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.1"],"relevance_strength":"weak","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0023","unit-0025"],"explanation":"PGR desafuero request (May 2004) for alleged abuse of authority and contempt of court related to land expropriation in Cuajimalpa (2000). Legal-constitutional conflict between federal and DF authorities. Weak relevance to 5B.1 through institutional governance quality, but primarily a political-legal dispute.","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0025","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.1"],"relevance_strength":"weak","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0024","unit-0026"],"explanation":"200,000 PRD supporters demonstrated in Zócalo supporting López Obrador (August 2004); published 'Un proyecto alternativo de nación' with 20 program points; presidential dismissal of Marcelo Ebrard (Security Secretary). Political mobilization and internal governance; weak relevance to economic policy content.","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0026","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.1"],"relevance_strength":"weak","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0025","unit-0027"],"explanation":"Congressional vote (April 2005): 360-127 in favor of desafuero; López Obrador called 'movimiento de resistencia civil pacífica.' Political-constitutional crisis; weak relevance to economic governance quality.","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0027","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.5"],"relevance_strength":"material","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0026","unit-0028"],"explanation":"Legal resolution: PGR unable to get judge to initiate proceedings (April 25, 2005); Fox accepted resignation of prosecutor Macedo de la Concha; new prosecutor Daniel Cabeza de Vaca withdrew charges (May 4); meeting between Fox and López Obrador; charges archived. Published 'Contra el desafuero; mi defensa jurídica.' Resolution of legal process for alleged contempt; relevant for institutional governance quality (5B.1) and rule of law (5B.5).","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0028","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.1","5B.2"],"relevance_strength":"weak","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0027","unit-0029"],"explanation":"PRD candidacy for 2006 presidential election: took leave from DF government (July 2005); Alejandro Encinas became acting head of government; Cárdenas withdrew from contention; López Obrador became sole precandidate (Sept 2005); registered as candidate of 'Coalición por el Bien de Todos' (Dec 2005). Campaign positioning; weak relevance to economic governance through candidate quality and platform statements.","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0029","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.1","5B.5"],"relevance_strength":"weak","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0028","unit-0030"],"explanation":"2006 campaign: accused Calderón of nepotism, abuse of functions, and traffic of influences as BANOBRAS director and Energy secretary; anti-FOBAPROA messaging ('privatización de las ganancias y socialización de las pérdidas'). Campaign accusations; weak substantive evidence on actual governance quality.","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0030","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.1","5B.5"],"relevance_strength":"weak","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0029","unit-0031"],"explanation":"Campaign program: diagnose of corruption and privilege 'from top to bottom'; commitment to halve presidential salary; fight tax fraud and evasion; austerity in government; investigation of FOBAPROA through a Commission of Truth. Policy statements; relevant to 5B.1 (prosperity agenda) and 5B.5 (anti-corruption commitment) but as campaign promises rather than implemented policy.","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0031","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.1","5B.3","5B.5","5B.8"],"relevance_strength":"material","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0030","unit-0032"],"explanation":"2006 campaign economic program: social development programs; extending public services to degraded areas; supporting agriculture, tourism, public works; protecting Pemex from any privatization; defending constitutional right to 'justo' wage; opposition to NAFTA privatization of agriculture; migration policy. Relevant for 5B.1 (spending priorities), 5B.3 (state enterprise protection), 5B.5 (anti-corruption), 5B.8 (distribution to vulnerable groups).","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0032","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.1"],"relevance_strength":"weak","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0031","unit-0033"],"explanation":"International relations positioning: no relationship with Chávez; distance from Bolivarian strategy; relationship with US based on mutual respect. Political positioning; weak relevance to economic governance.","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0033","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.1"],"relevance_strength":"weak","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0032","unit-0034"],"explanation":"Election night and PREP results: Calderón led by 0.64% (final margin 0.58% — 243,934 votes); López Obrador insisted he had different data showing victory. Electoral dispute; weak relevance to economic governance through political legitimacy.","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0034","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.1"],"relevance_strength":"weak","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0033","unit-0035"],"explanation":"Post-election mobilization: 'fraude a la antigüita,' 'retroceso democrático'; IFE and Fox accused; 'resistencia civil pacífica' including road blockades. Political mobilization after disputed election; weak governance relevance.","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0035","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.1"],"relevance_strength":"weak","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0034","unit-0036"],"explanation":"TEPJF ruling: ordered partial recount (9% of ballot boxes); López Obrador rejected ruling; called Calderón 'usurpador' and 'pelele'; intensified resistance. Electoral dispute continuation; weak governance relevance.","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0036","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0035","unit-0037"],"explanation":"September 2006: PRD attempted to sabotage Calderón inauguration; López Obrador's second marriage to Beatriz Gutiérrez Müller (October 16). Personal and ceremonial content; no economic governance relevance.","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0037","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.1"],"relevance_strength":"weak","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0036","unit-0038"],"explanation":"November 20, 2006: National Democratic Convention (CND) proclaimed López Obrador 'presidente legítimo' with cabinet of 12 'ministers'; ceremony in Zócalo with banda tricolor. Political legitimacy claim; weak governance relevance.","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0038","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.1"],"relevance_strength":"weak","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0037","unit-0039"],"explanation":"December 1, 2006 inauguration chaos; Calderón took oath in disputed ceremony; López Obrador led rival rally in Zócalo; published 'La mafia nos robó la Presidencia' (July 2007). Electoral dispute aftermath; weak economic governance relevance.","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0039","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.1"],"relevance_strength":"weak","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0038","unit-0040"],"explanation":"2007-2008 opposition period: continued defending legitimacy; maintained public profile; produced documentary 'Fraude: México 2006' (Mandoki).
